title: Microsoft 365 Backup: what is protected, for how long, and what it costs
summary: Hold: Microsoft documents beta automation for Full Workload Backup, contrary to the table and open question. The page also overstates protection against deletion outside offboarding and must specify mail-enabled security groups for notifications.

claims.claim: Tenant role assignments are reached through Identity > Roles & admins > role > Add assignments in Microsoft Entra admin center.
claims.quote: Browse to Identity > Roles & admins. ... Select a role name to open the role. ... Select Add assignments

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments assigns the Backup Administrator role.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments
claims.fix: Keep the call; append to the row note: 'The request body sets roleDefinitionId to the role definition, principalId to the assignee, and directoryScopeId to / for tenant scope.' The cited assignment page documents these properties.

claims.claim: Billing > Pay-as-you-go > Billing policies > Add a billing policy opens billing policy creation in Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: go to Billing > Pay-as-you-go. ... On the Billing policies tab, select Add a billing policy.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented automation for creating the Microsoft 365 Backup admin-center pay-as-you-go billing policies.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Backup pay-as-you-go billing policies budget Graph API PowerShell create update; "billing policy" "Microsoft 365 Backup" "New-SPO". Read billing-node setup, Backup setup and third-party billing results; New-SPOAppBillingPolicy concerns partner applications, not these policies.

claims.claim: Billing > Pay-as-you-go > policy > Budget > Settings > Set a budget for this policy reaches the budget control.
claims.quote: In the policy panel, select the Budget tab. ... select Settings. ... Select the Set a budget for this policy checkbox.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented Graph or PowerShell automation for these admin-center billing-policy budgets.
claims.quote: Searched: "Microsoft 365" "billing policies" "budget" "API" "Graph"; Microsoft 365 Backup pay-as-you-go billing policies budget Graph API PowerShell create update. Read billing-node budget steps, budget article results and Copilot Cost Management API overview; no matching budget operation.

claims.claim: Settings > Microsoft 365 Backup > SharePoint > Set up policy is the route to choosing protected SharePoint sites.
claims.quote: in the SharePoint section, select Set up policy. ... On the Choose selection method page ... Under Select sites individually, you can search and select sites
claims.fix: The path stops at the policy wizard entrance. For individual selection, extend it to 'Settings > Microsoft 365 Backup > SharePoint > Set up policy > Overview > Choose selection method > Select sites individually', as documented on the cited page.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/solutions/backupRestore/sharePointProtectionPolicies creates a policy with the selected sites.
claims.quote: siteProtectionUnits ... Collection of the siteProtectionUnits to be added to the sharePointProtectionPolicy object. Required.
claims.fix: Keep the call and append to the note: 'The request body sets siteProtectionUnits, with siteId identifying each selected site.' The cited reference documents that collection and shows siteId in the request.

claims.claim: Settings > Microsoft 365 Backup > Backup policies > policy > View details > Recovery window reaches the policy recovery-window setting.
claims.quote: select the Backup policies tab ... select that policy and then select View details. ... open an active policy, update the Recovery window

claims.claim: PATCH /v1.0/solutions/backupRestore/sharePointProtectionPolicies/{sharePointProtectionPolicyId} updates recovery-window retention through retentionSettings.
claims.quote: retentionSettings ... Updated retention settings for the policy. If retentionSettings is omitted, the existing retention settings are unchanged.

claims.claim: Settings > Microsoft 365 Backup > Back up sites > All sites selects Full Workload Backup for SharePoint.
claims.quote: On Microsoft 365 Backup dashboard, select Back up sites, and then choose All sites.

claims.claim: Full Workload Backup automation and the beta policy cmdlet's required ProtectionMode value are not documented.
claims.quote: When set to fullServiceBackup, the entire workload is backed up and specific sites can be excluded using exclusion units.
claims.fix: Replace controls[5].api with kind 'powershell', call 'New-MgBetaSolutionBackupRestoreSharePointProtectionPolicy -ProtectionMode fullServiceBackup', and docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoft.graph.beta.backuprestore/new-mgbetasolutionbackuprestoresharepointprotectionpolicy?view=graph-powershell-beta'. The cmdlet reference lists -ProtectionMode, and https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/resources/sharepointprotectionpolicy?view=graph-rest-beta defines its value. Note that this is beta automation, subject to change and not supported for production use. Remove the first Open questions bullet and cite both references.

claims.claim: Settings > Microsoft 365 Backup > Email notifications reaches notification configuration.
claims.quote: Select Settings. ... Select Microsoft 365 Backup ... Go to the Email notifications option on the Microsoft 365 Backup home page.

claims.claim: Update-MgSolutionBackupRestoreEmailNotificationSetting -IsEnabled -Recipients <IMicrosoftGraphNotificationRecipients> enables notifications and sets their recipients.
claims.quote: [-IsEnabled] ... [-Recipients <IMicrosoftGraphNotificationRecipients>] ... Indicates whether notifications are enabled.

claims.claim: Assigning the role requires at least Privileged Role Administrator.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center as at least a Privileged Role Administrator.

claims.claim: Customers onboarded before April 1, 2026 may retain the older Setup billing experience.
claims.quote: Existing customers who onboarded to Backup before April 1, 2026 ... can now migrate their billing management from Setup tab

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Backup provides point-in-time recovery for SharePoint sites, OneDrive accounts and Exchange Online mailboxes.
claims.quote: Full SharePoint site and OneDrive account restore fidelity ... at specific prior points in time via a rollback operation. ... Full Exchange mailbox item restores or granular item restores

claims.claim: Backup supports recovery after accidental deletion, malicious overwrite and ransomware.
claims.quote: a ransomware attack ... or instances of an internal accidental or malicious data deletion or overwrite event

claims.quote: The Microsoft 365 Backup service, offered through the Microsoft 365 admin center

claims.where: What it is, opening; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Backup charges by consumption rather than by user.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Backup is a pay-as-you-go offering that charges based on consumption, unlike traditional user-based licenses.

claims.claim: Administrators create backup policies separately for each product.
claims.quote: you need to create a backup policy for each product. A policy represents the backup plan defined by admins

claims.claim: Protection units include SharePoint sites, OneDrive accounts and Exchange Online mailboxes.
claims.quote: Protection units - SharePoint sites, OneDrive accounts, Exchange Online mailboxes, or supported Microsoft Entra ID directory objects backed up by the Microsoft 365 Backup tool.

claims.where: What it is, Backup policies; controls[5].governs; What to check
claims.claim: Full Workload Backup automatically protects eligible units not covered by custom policies, including new units.
claims.quote: all eligible SharePoint sites, OneDrive accounts, or Exchange mailboxes ... that aren't already protected by another backup policy. ... any new protection units are automatically protected.

claims.claim: Full Workload Backup supports an exclusion list.
claims.quote: You can also maintain an exclusion list to keep specific protection units out of Full Workload Backup protection.

claims.quote: Custom backup policies always take precedence over Full Workload Backup.

claims.where: What it is, Recovery window; summary; controls[4].governs
claims.claim: The recovery window is set per policy and determines recovery-point retention.
claims.quote: The Recovery window determines how long Microsoft 365 Backup keeps recovery points ... You set the recovery window on a policy

claims.claim: SharePoint and OneDrive recovery windows can be 3 months, 6 months or whole years from 1 through 10.
claims.quote: SharePoint and OneDrive: 3 months, 6 months, 1 year, 2 years, 3 years, 4 years, 5 years, 6 years, 7 years, 8 years, 9 years, or 10 years.

claims.claim: Exchange recovery windows can be 3 months, 6 months, 1 year or 2 years.
claims.quote: Exchange: 3 months, 6 months, 1 year, or 2 years.

claims.claim: Existing SharePoint, OneDrive and Exchange policies default to a one-year recovery window.
claims.quote: For SharePoint, OneDrive, and Exchange Online, existing policies and artifacts default to a 1-year recovery window.

claims.claim: Administrators cannot change backup frequency.
claims.quote: The backup frequency isn't currently variable or modifiable.

claims.claim: Full SharePoint site and OneDrive account restore points have ten-minute frequency within the last 14 days.
claims.quote: Type | RPO for 0-14 days in the past ... Full OneDrive account and full SharePoint site restore | 10 minutes

claims.claim: Full SharePoint site and OneDrive account recovery points are weekly beyond 14 days.
claims.quote: One week, through the configured recovery window of up to 10 years

claims.claim: Exchange recovery points have ten-minute frequency throughout its recovery window.
claims.quote: Exchange Online | 10 minutes | 10 minutes
claims.fix: Replace 'Exchange has 10-minute points throughout' with 'The restore documentation gives Exchange 10-minute points both within and beyond 14 days; the overview table instead describes 10-minute points for the prior 52 weeks.' Both https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/backup/backup-restore-data and https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/backup/backup-overview are already cited.

claims.claim: Restoration can target the original location, replacing existing data, or a new location.
claims.quote: restore data either at the original location (replacing existing data at that location) or at a new location.

claims.claim: Backup content remains inside the Microsoft 365 data trust boundary.
claims.quote: Data never leaves the Microsoft 365 data trust boundary and honors the geographic locations of your current data residency.

claims.where: What it is, Storage; Risks and limits, immutability
claims.claim: SharePoint, OneDrive and Exchange backups use append-only storage to prevent overwrites.
claims.quote: Our backups are protected from malicious overwrites because OneDrive, SharePoint, and Exchange use Append-Only backup storage.

claims.where: What it is, Storage; Why it matters; Risks and limits, immutability
claims.claim: Backups are deleted only when an administrator offboards them.
claims.quote: Decreasing the recovery window is a destructive action, because recovery points older than the new window are deleted. ... the deletion takes effect only after a 30-day grace period
claims.fix: Replace the Storage sentence with 'Backups stay inside the Microsoft 365 data trust boundary in append-only storage; recovery points expire under the recovery window, and offboarding can also delete backups.' Replace 'Backups are immutable except through offboarding' with 'Append-only storage prevents backup overwrites; decreasing a recovery window can delete older recovery points after a 30-day grace period.' In Why it matters, change 'offboarding does' to 'the backup recovery window and offboarding govern their lifetime'. The policy page documents window reductions, including moving an artifact to a shorter-window policy; the offboarding page also documents billing-triggered offboarding.

claims.where: What it is, Storage; Why it matters
claims.claim: Purview retention and deletion policies do not change the backup recovery window.
claims.quote: Retention and deletion policies (for example, from Purview) don't affect the backup recovery window, which remains fully isolated from those policies.

claims.claim: Microsoft Entra Backup and Recovery protects directory objects.
claims.quote: back up all or select SharePoint sites, OneDrive accounts, Exchange mailboxes, and Entra directory objects
